noteBlocks.md:
**1.** Sperm are made in the **testis**, which hangs in the **scrotum** outside the body.
**2.** The **sperm tube** carries them away from the testis.
**3.** The **prostate gland** adds fluid; sperm plus that fluid is **semen**.
**4.** The semen leaves along the **urethra**, which runs through the **penis**.

The prostate gland is the junction: sperm tube before it, urethra after it.

noteBlocks.explain: The sperm tube. CCEA prints 'sperm tube'; other books call it the vas deferens, and either is accepted, but write the one on the specification.

noteBlocks.title: Why the scrotum hangs outside
noteBlocks.md:
Sperm are made best at a temperature a little **below** body temperature, so the testes are kept outside the body cavity where it is cooler. That is the whole reason, and it is worth a mark on its own.

One warning about the **urethra**. It is the only tube in the body that carries semen at one time and urine at another — but never both at once. Nothing else here touches urine: urine is made in the **kidney** and carried down by the **ureter**, which is a different tube with an almost identical name.

noteBlocks.prompt: What does the prostate gland do?
noteBlocks.explain: It adds fluid to the sperm, and sperm plus that fluid is semen. Answers to this question drift towards urine more than anything else on the paper.

noteBlocks.md:
**1.** The **ovary** releases one **ovum**, about once a month.
**2.** The **oviduct** catches it in its fringed funnel and carries it along. **This is where fertilisation happens.**
**3.** The ovum reaches the **uterus**, whose thick lining is where an embryo could settle.

Below the uterus is the **cervix**, a ring of muscle, and below that the **vagina**.

noteBlocks.title: Other books, other names
noteBlocks.md:
Other books call the sperm tube the **vas deferens** and the oviduct the **Fallopian tube**. Same structures. CCEA prints **sperm tube** and **oviduct**, so write those.

The **epididymis**, the **seminal vesicles**, **FSH** and **LH** belong to other specifications, not this one.

noteBlocks.prompt: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilisation take place?
noteBlocks.explain: The oviduct. The ovum is fertilised on its way from the ovary to the uterus; the uterus is where the ball of cells settles afterwards.

**Step 1 — read the command word.** It asks for the **function**, not the name.

**Step 3 — D is the gland around the top of the urethra**: it *adds fluid to the sperm to make semen*. **[1]**
**Step 4 — check.** Neither answer mentions urine.

noteBlocks.md:
Diagrams in books are printed at a **scale**. Half life size means the drawing is half as long as the real thing, so the real thing is **twice** the drawing.

An oviduct measures 55 mm on a diagram printed at half life size. Real length = drawn ÷ magnification = 55 ÷ 0.5 = 110 mm, which is 11.0 cm.

Divide, never multiply, when the drawing is smaller than the real thing — and read the unit on the answer line.

noteBlocks.prompt: A uterus measures 40 mm across on a diagram printed at half life size. How wide is it really, in millimetres?
noteBlocks.explain: 40 ÷ 0.5 = 80 mm. Half life size means the real thing is twice the drawing.

Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Six structures, in order: two of them make or hold, one carries, one adds, and two lead out.
Give each structure a job in the same sentence as its name.
parts.workedSolution: Sperm are made in the testis. The testes hang in the scrotum, a sac outside the body, because sperm are made best at a temperature a little below body temperature. From the testis the sperm are carried away along the sperm tube. On the way, the prostate gland adds fluid to the sperm; sperm and that fluid together are called semen. The semen then passes out along the urethra, which is the same tube that carries urine at other times. The urethra runs the length of the penis, and the penis places the semen inside the vagina.

commonErrors.feedback: Ureter and urethra are the near-identical pair the mark scheme will not let through. The ureter runs from the kidney to the bladder; the tube that carries semen out through the penis is the urethra.

prompts.prompt: Name the six parts of the male reproductive system the specification lists.
prompts.answer: Testis, scrotum, sperm tube, prostate gland, urethra and penis.

prompts.prompt: What does the prostate gland do?
prompts.answer: It adds fluid to the sperm. Sperm and that fluid together are called semen.

prompts.prompt: The urethra and the ureter are two different tubes. What does each one carry, and where does it run?
prompts.answer: The urethra carries semen and, at other times, urine, and runs from the bladder out through the penis. The ureter carries urine only, from the kidney down to the bladder.

prompts.prompt: Name the five parts of the female reproductive system the specification lists.
prompts.answer: Ovary, oviduct, uterus, cervix and vagina.

prompts.prompt: Where does fertilisation happen, and where does the ball of cells settle afterwards?
prompts.answer: Fertilisation happens in the oviduct. The ball of cells settles into the lining of the uterus.

prompts.prompt: Why are the testes held in the scrotum, outside the body?
prompts.answer: Because it is cooler outside the body, and sperm are made best at a temperature a little below body temperature.
